## TL;DR

Reviewed Mission Control at desktop and phone widths in headless WebKit against the task worktree's auth-less server. The page stayed within both viewports, the resource sparklines rendered after a second live sample, and forced service errors appeared in the usage and decision panels without browser errors. Fixed the process table's narrow layout by preserving readable columns inside a horizontally scrollable region. Added a focused responsive test and recorded the pass in `docs/qa/2026-11-control-dashboard.md`.

## Work and rationale

I began by reading the task copy in this worktree and checking the dashboard composition. Mission Control is assembled from AI usage, system resources, six status cards, auto-engineering, releases, live activity, decisions, and attention. The panels use different data paths: API calls, server-sent resource samples, board state, and repository tasks. I inspected those boundaries and their empty/error branches before running the app.

The process table was the concrete responsive defect. It lays out PID, task, CPU, memory, runtime, and a kill action in six grid columns. At narrow widths, those columns had no minimum width and their parent did not scroll horizontally. This let the row shrink to the phone's content width, making the operational data difficult to read. The fix keeps the parent within the panel, enables inline horizontal scrolling, and gives both header and rows a 560px minimum width. Desktop layout remains unchanged because the content naturally fits the wider container.

I added `control-dashboard-responsive.test.ts`. It checks the CSS contract and uses headless WebKit to render a representative process header and row at 375px and 1280px. At 375px, the test verifies the scroller remains within the available page width while its contents retain the readable minimum. At 1280px it verifies the row fits without activating horizontal overflow.

The QA record covers the live empty usage and activity states, the attention panel empty and populated states, populated release entries, six status cards, system metrics, the pressure alert, and the process list. I let the live resource sampler emit a second sample and verified both CPU and memory sparkline paths appeared. For failure handling, I intercepted the board usage and decision requests and returned HTTP 503 at 375px. The usage panel showed its unavailable text and Retry action, while the decision panel showed the service error.

## Approaches tried

I first inspected component templates and media rules to identify a specific regression before changing code. Then I ran `bun run build`, started `just serve-noauth 7272` from the task worktree, and opened it only with headless WebKit. I measured document and process-table dimensions at both target viewports, checked browser console and page errors, and captured local screenshots under ignored `.repoos/` for visual inspection. I separately intercepted API failures so an error-state pass did not depend on the live server being broken.

## Challenges and blockers

System resource sparklines intentionally need more than one sample. The first page load showed current metrics but no path yet, so I waited for the next five-second server sample and checked that both paths were then present. The live activity feed remained empty, which exercised its intended empty copy; decision and attention data changed during the run, so I recorded the observed empty and populated cases without treating that change as an application failure.

The live server had no recorded AI usage, which gave a truthful empty case but not representative non-zero token and cost rows. I did not substitute invented live data. The error case used a controlled browser route and is described as such in the QA record.

## Key learnings

The dashboard already has appropriate empty and failure feedback in the usage and decisions panels, and the ordinary live page remained stable even when those API calls failed. The resource metrics are event-driven rather than synchronously populated at mount; chart verification needs at least two SSE samples. For dense tabular data, containment belongs on the table wrapper while columns keep a minimum readable width. That keeps the page itself at 375px and gives users access to every field by scrolling the table region.
